tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H53): Balanced token-range GEMM1 tiles under the H49 image counters (one tile per CTA) on the wide-C rows, with a 10-minute cache-hint test first. You built H49 last round; continue from that tc-only source and the < 2 s str.replace build loop. STEP 0 (H56, cap 10 B200 minutes): compile-time HINTS variants of the shipped tc_kernel: (a) none, (b) createpolicy.fractional evict_first on the one-pass reads (x plane cp.async.bulk .L2::cache_hint, fp32 W1/W2 LDG via ld.global.L2::cache_hint), (c) b plus evict_last on the fp16 weight scratch stores, the h' stores and the out red.add / bulk reduce. Only our own buffers, no applypriority, no discard. harness_time interleaved x3 at 16,384, 8,768 and 32,768. Keep a variant only if it is >= 0.7 us faster on two rows and no row is > 0.3 us slower; record the numbers either way. STEP 1 (H53): replace the whole-image GEMM1 tile tables by static token-range tables where a tile = (hidden block, contiguous token range) that may straddle images. In the epilogue, split each thread's per-(image,k) sumsq at the static image boundaries of its range (the r10 tc2 code has this split), red.add the partials into the per-image gsum, publish on each image's counter (target = number of tiles touching that image, static per row), then wait on every image the tile touches before pass 2. Keep fp32 h in its TMEM columns as in r12. Tables to start from: 16,384 12 hidden x 12 ranges of 261-262 tokens (N=264 as two MMAs of 136+128, 144 CTAs, 1 tile each); 8,384 12 x 12 of 130-131 (N=136); 16,768 24 x 6 of 130-131; 8,768 24 x 6 of 65-66 (N=72); 32,768 24 x 6 of 261-262 (N=264) vs 24 x 12 of 130-131 (2 tiles per CTA, image-major so wave-1 groups complete in wave 1); 2,768 24 x 6 of 16-17 (N=24) as a stretch. Price each table with the H31 port rule max(N/2, (4096+32N)/123) clk per k16 before you build it. Deadlock freedom: every tile publishes before it waits, and with 2 tiles per CTA the first tiles of all CTAs cover whole image groups. STEP 2: stamp pass 1 / wait / pass 2 / GEMM1 end per row against the parent. Then re-tune the GEMM2 unit tables for 148 busy CTAs (KS/MP, the r12 sweep method). STEP 3: run_tests 16/16 including the portal-order re-runs; a fresh 10-round fp64 precision log on every changed row (the gf summation order changes); a 400-call NaN-prefilled counter stress at 16,384 and 32,768; cuobjdump STACK 0 on every instantiation. Compare each row against r12-merge's path for that row (16,384 is tc2, 32,768 is H49, the rest are r11 tc), interleaved x3 in one container. If the gate is missed, ship the best per-row table you measured with its numbers, never a placeholder. Success: Same container, interleaved x3 vs r12-merge: 16,384 <= -3 us AND 8,384 <= -1.5 us, AND at least one of 32,768 / 16,768 / 8,768 <= -1 us; 16/16 pass, 0 beyond-atol elements in the 10-round log, STACK 0 Refuted if: 16,384 and 8,384 are both within 0.5 us of r12-merge with one-tile-per-CTA tables, i.e. the per-tile fixed costs (accumulator wait, image wait, publish) cancel the balance This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). A missed gate or success line is not a reason to stop: switch to the best configuration your own probes found (or the experiment's next variant), build it into a full kernel and measure it with run_tests, and use the rest of the budget on it. Hand in a measured kernel that implements this experiment's design on at least one workload (others may fall back); the r0 baseline or the unchanged parent is not a valid candidate unless a measured hardware fact rules the design out (name it, with the probe's number). Record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid, cluster or per-image counters (and departure counters) live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value and a per-shape cuBLASLt heuristic; cache hints (createpolicy, L2::cache_hint, evict_first/evict_last) only on our own workspace buffers (h', d16, the fp16 weight scratch), never on x, the weights or the output tensor; timing-only stubs that skip work are never the shipped candidate; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build.

Experiment E2 (tests H54): All-warp strip conv with coalesced stores and 512 threads for sc_kernel (and the 14x14 tc conv), then the skewed-arrival barrier A/B. Continue from your r12 sc-only fast loop (7 variants in 5.6 s through ctypes). STEP 1: rebuild sc_kernel's phase-A conv. Split each zero-padded smem plane into row strips; a warp owns one strip of one plane and each lane computes a register-blocked output segment (1x4 or 1x7), with the 49 taps and dwb in registers. Deal the items round-robin over ALL warps of all 148 CTAs (28 CTAs are idle at 1,192 today). Keep the plane copies as they are: the r12 NS sweep showed more copies lose, so the gain must come from more warps per landed plane. Keep the per-output tap summation order unchanged so the roundings do not change. Combine with your coalesced store path (d16 staged in smem, lane-contiguous 16-B stores of d16 and of out = x + b2' from the landed plane). Stamp conv end minus planes landed at 1,192, 2,96, 4,192 and 8,192, interleaved x3 against the parent. STEP 2: with regs at ~107, build sc_kernel with __launch_bounds__(512,1) and run the GEMM1 epilogue and GEMM2 drain on all 16 warps (the tc_kernel all-warp pattern, H36). Check STACK 0 on <192,28,16>, <96,56,4> and <160,7,4>, and keep 512 threads only where it is faster. STEP 3: stamp tc_kernel<384,196>'s conv (8,384 / 16,384) after its planes land. If it is > 2 us, apply the same item split there and time it. STEP 4 (H52): on the rebuilt sc_kernel, A/B cg grid.sync against a single monotonic-counter barrier. All CTAs red.add one counter; the target is computed from the returned value as (old / N + 1) * N, there is no reset cell, and arrivals poll with ld.acquire on the same line; the counter must stay correct for every call (no other cross-call state). Interleave x3 on all 7 sc rows and record the release maxima. STEP 5: run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs. Precision: if the conv arithmetic is unchanged, cite the r8 log plus a single-seed fp64 check per row; any change in rounding or summation means a fresh 10-round log (sc rows sit at 79-89 % of atol). Rows under 40 us move about 1 us between portal submissions, so judge by the interleaved rented deltas, and note that the merge needs 3 % projected gain on a row. Success: Conv after landing <= 1.6 us at 1,192 and <= 6 us at 8,192; at least 3 of {2,96, 4,192, 8,192, 4,96, 1,160} faster than r12-merge by >= 1.5 us rented in the same container (interleaved x3); 16/16 pass; STACK 0 Refuted if: The conv-after-landing segment shrinks by < 25 % at both 1,192 and 8,192 with all warps busy (then the conv is LDS/halo-bound, not occupancy-bound) This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. Experiment E3 (tests H43): Ship lineage I's tcgen05 pass 1 as full 64,96 and 32,128 rows (K0 + pass 1 + K3 + cuBLASLt swap-AB G2) with the precision log. Incubation continuation; build on your 547 us pass 1. STEP 1: attach the notebook tail that G r7/r8 shipped: K0 (weight prep and gsum zeroing in the same call), K3 (per-image fp16 W2_b = s_b * W2 plus b2' hi/lo columns, from red.add per-tile sums, __launch_bounds__(512,2), W2 row loaded up front) and the cuBLASLt batched swap-AB GEMM2 (beta 1 onto x, heuristic top-1). Make sure your pass 1 writes the K-augmentation rows that GEMM2 expects. STEP 2: instantiate the 32,128 configuration (4C=512). STEP 3: run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs (only 64,96 and 32,128 routed to the new path, everything else on the r0 anchor as merge-only), plus a 10-round fp64 precision log on both rows (harness generators, seed 200; count the max |err| and the elements beyond each row's own atol). Wrap harness_time in a retry, because the CUPTI first-kernel drop happens on multi-launch paths. STEP 4, only if time remains (pool I28 skeleton test): a timing-only variant with W1' out of smem (garbage A) and NS = 5/6 x-ring stages against NS = 3 at 64,96. Report the skeleton time; go further only if it is <= 180 us. Do not hand in a placeholder: if a row loses, ship the other row and report both. Success: Same container vs r12-merge: 64,96 <= 780 us and 32,128 <= 215 us rented (G ~860 / ~228), 0 beyond-atol in the 10-round log on both rows, 16/16 pass Refuted if: Neither row beats r12-merge by >= 5 % rented with the full tail (pass 1 gain eaten by the tail or the cuBLASLt G2 fallback) This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. Experiment E4 (tests H55): New design: token-stationary one-launch tcgen05 kernel for the C=96 rows with resident weights, TMEM-resident hidden and per-image GRN counters. Build from scratch for 1,96,56,56, 2,96,56,56 and 4,96,56,56 (route only these rows; the r0 anchor serves the other rows as merge-only). Use the notebook recipes: H's engine recipe, D's SW128 descriptor values, G's writer address functions for the MN-major B tile, and H49's counters with departure reset. Validate the tcgen05 engine against torch before anything else. Structure: one cooperative launch. Each CTA owns a 64-token range (1,96: 49 CTAs; 2,96: 98) or a 128-token range (4,96: 98 CTAs); ranges may straddle images at 4,96. Entry: issue the x strip copies with their 3-row halos (3-D TMA box with OOB zero fill, start w = -4) and the fp32 W1 copy. Convert W1 to fp16 with the LN-weight fold, u and v row sums into resident K-major SW128 A (72 KB), with no scratch and no sync. Run the conv on all warps straight into the MN-major SW128 d tile, with the LN statistics per token. GEMM1 swap-AB: three 128-hidden M blocks x N tokens into TMEM (384 columns). Epilogue: LN fold, A&S erfc GELU, fp32 h back into TMEM (tcgen05.st), sumsq per (image,k) red.add, publish, and wait on the image counter(s). While waiting, land and convert fp32 W2 into resident fp16 A (72 KB, reusing W1's space). After the wait: h' = fp16(h * (1 + gw*gf*inv_b)) into an smem B tile (or into TMEM as the A operand, if you choose the token-major form of pool I30), then GEMM2 into the remaining 128 TMEM columns, and out = x + acc + b2' (b2' = W2.gb + b2 in fp32) stored NCHW with lanes along hw. The hidden is rounded once. STEP 0 gate: a stub with all data movement, MMAs and the counter wait but no epilogue maths, at 2,96 and 1,96 after the 252 MB flush, stamped per phase. Your projection is ~10-11 us at 2,96, and the gate is the stub within 1.5x of the projection for its part. Hardware premise to measure first: per-CTA ingest plus conversion of the 295 KB of fp32 weights at 98 co-resident CTAs <= 4 us. If it is above, switch to the fallback (grid-wide fp16 weight scratch plus one counter sync) instead of stopping. Price the N=64 MMAs with the H31 port rule. If the gate is missed, build and measure the best fallback configuration, never a placeholder. Finish with run_tests 16/16 (portal-order re-runs), a 10-round fp64 precision log on each shipped row, a 400-call counter stress, STACK 0, and an interleaved x3 timing against r12-merge (D sc). New lineages need a 10 % projected gain for the merge to take a row. Stretch only if everything above is done: 1,160,449,7 (410 KB of weights) behind the same gate. Success: 2,96 <= 17 us and 4,96 <= 28 us rented in the same container (D sc 25.0 / 37.6), 1,96 <= 14 (18.2); 16/16 pass, 0 beyond-atol in the 10-round log, STACK 0 Refuted if: The full kernel is not faster than D's sc_kernel at both 2,96 and 4,96 after the gate stub met its projection (the chain, not the ingest, then binds a token-stationary design) This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%.
